sentences.text:
(3) Contends that petitioner is in custody since 15.02.2024; he has not been named in the FIR;
rather has been falsely implicated during investigation in the present case by showing false recovery of Rs.25,000/- from him.
Also contends that petitioner, who is working as Motor Mechanic, has not committed any offence.

(4) Per contra, learned State Counsel, on instructions from I.O./ASI Pardeep, opposed the prayer while submitting that petitioner was part of well organized racket, which is involved in duping innocent people by getting their hard-earned money transferred in their bank account(s).
(5) Heard learned Counsel for the parties and perused the paper- book.

(6) The petitioner was granted interim bail by this Court on 25.09.2024 and the matter has been adjourned from time to time on request of the parties; therefore, interim bail is continuously extended.

(7) Although, petitioner is stated to be in custody since 15.02.2024; but perusal of para 6 & 11 of the affidavit reveals that apart from Rs.25,000/-, the mobile phone and SIM Card used in the present fraud were also found to be recovered from the petitioner.
2 of 3 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:166377 (8) In view of the above, complicity of the petitioner is, prima facie, apparent.

Thus, no ground is made out to grant him the concession of bail pending trial "at this stage".
(9) Accordingly, the present petition is dismissed.
(10) Needless to say that interim order dated 25.09.2024, extended from time to time, shall come to an end, automatically.
(11) The above observations may not be construed as an expression of opinion on merits of the present case in any manner.

Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed off.
12th December, 2024 ( MAHABIR SINGH SINDHU )
Gagan JUDGE
